work_candidate.original_synopsis: The da Vinci arrives at the Tellarite colony Kharzh'ulla IV to inspect a colossal ring-shaped orbital habitat and space elevators damaged during the Dominion War. A temporary strengthening-field repair has made one elevator too rigid, risking the collapse of the entire system. Tev, who grew up on Kharzh'ulla, resists confronting the place where his mother died in an elevator accident and a former friend gained status by taking credit for his scholarly work. After replacement components prove inadequate, Tev devises a controlled collapse of the damaged elevator to preserve the Ring. He discreetly persuades the colony's transportation minister to present the idea as his own so the government will accept it. Detachment triggers an unexpected premature breakup, forcing Gold's crew to improvise with tractors and torpedoes; part of the shaft falls into the ocean while the main portion is pulled away, and the Ring remains in orbit. The colony avoids the projected catastrophe. Tev forgoes public credit, and Gomez learns the extent of the authorship and exclusion that shaped his departure.

chapter_spans.original_summary: Tev's vivid nightmare relives his mother's fatal elevator-car accident, but the opening disaster is not happening in the present. Gomez refuses his request to avoid the Kharzh'ulla mission.

Tev briefs the crew on the orbital Ring, Dominion War damage and catastrophic failure scenarios. An ancient Fury origin is presented through archaeological interpretation and competing design hypotheses, not settled history.

Gomez and Tev meet transportation minister Eevraith and aging First Minister Grevesh. Eevraith's defensive explanation of temporary integrity-field supports and his tension with Tev leave feasibility and motives in dispute.

At the damaged elevator and factory the engineers find incomplete replacement panels. Tev visits a memorial to the crash that killed his mother, sharing personal grief and his perception of an earlier Fury-induced fear experience.

Gomez hears passages of Eevraith's celebrated technical dissertation that resemble Tev's language. She privately asks linguist Faulwell to investigate authorship instead of publicly asserting plagiarism.

The da Vinci engineers conclude that the temporary integrity field worsened cracking and a durable patch will not suffice. Tev suggests intentionally separating and collapsing the damaged elevator to save the remaining Ring, provided local leaders choose the plan.

Tev privately persuades Eevraith through political incentives and reveals an old conflict involving Biyert. Eevraith presents Tev's solution as his own to Grevesh, enabling the government to commission the controlled collapse.

Tev suffers zero-gravity distress while attaching charges, then undergoes medical assessment. Grevesh watches preparations from the bridge, while crew on the ground notice the elevator begin listing earlier than scheduled.

Detachment and sudden recoil apparently trigger premature charges. The da Vinci uses torpedoes and tractors to separate and divert the shaft; pieces strike ocean, the larger section is released far from Kharzh'ulla, and crew report Ring stability.

Eevraith privately thanks Tev without publicly acknowledging the plan's origin. Faulwell reports stylistic clues in Eevraith's dissertation and Tev confirms its authorship, explaining social exclusion and why he relinquished credit; the narrative ends before biography.

evidence.observation: The apparent present-time transport catastrophe is a recurrent nightmare; Tev later associates it with his deceased mother and personal fears, not a current incident.
The crew reviews extensive Ring damage and hazards; Tev and Gomez discuss Fury-origin archaeological indications and alternative strategic purposes without establishing unique builders or motives.

Eevraith says structurally strengthening the shaft increased stresses on its other sections and reveals gaps in preparedness; Grevesh's earlier ignorance and response are witnessed, their motives not omnisciently fixed.
Engineers inspect insufficient or non-custom replacement panels; Tev identifies his mother's accident memorial and attributes some of his nightmares to an earlier Fury fear weapon experience.
Gomez notices familiar phrasing in Eevraith's claimed dissertation and requests Faulwell's linguistic assessment; this is not yet proven academic authorship or legal wrongdoing.
Gomez, Tev and Gold consider evacuation after irreparable stresses, then propose detaching and deliberately dropping one elevator as an alternative requiring local consent.
Tev offers the controlled-collapse idea to Eevraith; Eevraith communicates it to Grevesh as his own, with Starfleet participation allowing local political acceptance.
Tev's symptoms are registered by suit telemetry and evaluated by Lense; separate ground observers see the shaft list unexpectedly before the planned detonation.
Crew infer release rebound caused premature detonations. Torpedoes divide the elevator, the lower pieces fall at sea, the long section is moved away, and ship sensors report the Ring stable.

Faulwell identifies hidden bilingual patterns in Eevraith's dissertation, Tev explicitly says he wrote it, and he describes social exclusion and a past bargain; no external legal adjudication of authorship appears.

assertions.subject: sce37:structure:ring
assertions.value: Fury manufacture is inferred from source-internal archaeological comparisons, but their origins, purposes and definitive identity as the builders remain open.

assertions.subject: sce37:structure:damaged-elevator
assertions.value: Engineering diagnosis attributes additional damage to excessive rigidity; this is in-story technical assessment, not an externally measured engineering result.

assertions.subject: sce37:person:tev
assertions.value: Mother's fatal accident is recalled and memorialized, while opening disaster is Tev's nightmare; the later described Fury-fear episode is his testimony, not a present-time repeat.

assertions.subject: sce37:person:eevraith
assertions.value: Tev proposes the strategy and allows Eevraith to present it as local ministerial initiative; future public attribution remains unestablished.

assertions.subject: sce37:structure:ring
assertions.value: Ship sensors report the Ring stable and the larger damaged shaft released into a trajectory away from the colony; the entire Ring is not shown fully repaired.

assertions.subject: sce37:person:eevraith
assertions.value: Faulwell's linguistic clues and Tev's direct admission support Tev as the source-local author, while Eevraith's formal degree or legal status is not independently adjudicated.

assertions.subject: sce37:place:kharzhulla-iv
assertions.value: Tev attributes his professional exclusion to being an outsider despite shared Tellarite species; his recollection is a perspective, not a population-wide sociological survey.
